candidates.title: How Amplitude ships product improvements in 1–2 days with OpenAI
candidates.summary: Built primarily on OpenAI models, Amplitude’s proactive product agent, Wave, identifies what to build, helps teams ship changes with coding agents, and measures the impact.

candidates.title: Building a self-service LLM gateway with Amazon Bedrock and LiteLLM
candidates.summary: Build a self-service LLM gateway with LiteLLM on AWS Fargate that puts Amazon Bedrock foundation models behind an OpenAI-compatible API. Developers get instant access through a single API key, while platform teams gain per-user cost controls, quota isolation, and observability.

candidates.title: Shield helps technicians hand off legacy portal work with OpenAI
candidates.summary: Shield uses OpenAI to help IT technicians hand off work in legacy portals. Its Forge agents navigate systems so technicians can focus on issues needing their judgment.

candidates.title: Optimizing cost per task and proving agent ROI on Amazon Bedrock
candidates.summary: Comparing per-token prices hides the real cost of running a model on Amazon Bedrock. This post shows how to calculate the true cost per task across four hidden cost drivers, reduce it with caching, routing, and output constraints, and prove agent ROI with human baselines, holdout experiments, and a five-dimension scorecard.

candidates.title: Google Search gets a major upgrade with Gemini 4 Hydrogen
candidates.summary: We are bringing Gemini 4 Hydrogen to Google Search globally to provide you with more helpful, visual, and intuitive responses.
